narration.heading: How big?
narration.text: You think Jupiter is as big as planets get? Think again.

narration.heading: Earth
narration.text: Start with Earth, the biggest and heaviest of the four rocky planets.

narration.heading: Neptune
narration.text: Neptune is about four times wider. Big, but nowhere near the record.

narration.heading: Jupiter
narration.text: Jupiter is about eleven times wider than Earth. A thousand Earths could fit inside.

narration.heading: WASP-17b
narration.text: Now leave the solar system. WASP-17b, about a thousand light-years away, is nearly twice Jupiter's width.

narration.heading: Backwards
narration.text: It even orbits backwards, against its star's spin. And the Webb telescope found clouds made of quartz.

narration.heading: HAT-P-67b
narration.text: HAT-P-67b is bigger still, over twice as wide as Jupiter, twelve hundred light-years away.

narration.heading: The twist
narration.text: The twist? It has under half of Jupiter's mass. It's less dense than a marshmallow.

narration.heading: Your turn
narration.text: So bigger isn't always heavier. What's the strangest planet you know?

hook.banner: How big can planets really get?

skit.text: Huge but weighs almost nothing? Like my promises to stop buffering.

titles: What if you lined up the biggest planets ever found?
The planet that's less dense than a marshmallow
youtube.description: Earth, Neptune and Jupiter side by side at true scale with two giant exoplanets, WASP-17b and HAT-P-67b, and why the biggest of them weighs less than Jupiter.

sources.claim: Earth's equatorial radius is 6,378.137 km; of the four rocky planets it is the largest and most massive
Neptune's equatorial diameter is 49,528 km, about four times wider than Earth
Jupiter's radius is 69,911 km, about 11 times Earth's width; about 1,000 Earths would fit inside
WASP-17b, about 1,000 light-years away, is about 1.9 times Jupiter's radius; it was the first planet found with a retrograde orbit; JWST detected evidence of quartz clouds in 2023
HAT-P-67b's host star is 1,200 light-years away; the planet is about 2.14 Jupiter radii and 0.45 Jupiter masses, with a density lower than marshmallows
